ASME B16.20 covers metallic gaskets for pipe flanges, including ring-joint gaskets; API 6A and API 6B/6BX define the ring-joint flange grooves for API flanges. Ring-joint gaskets deform into the groove when the flange is made up, so a new ring is fitted each time the joint is broken.

faqs.q: Which flanges does the BX-151 ring joint gasket fit?
faqs.a: The BX-151 ring joint gasket fits API 6BX: 1-13/16″ at 10,000, 15,000 and 20,000 psi. It is a pressure-energised Style BX ring supplied new in soft iron, low carbon steel, stainless steel or corrosion-resistant alloy.

faqs.q: What does the number in BX-151 mean on a ring joint gasket?
faqs.a: BX-151 is a Style BX ring and the number identifies one ring size and groove. The BX-151 has an outside diameter of 3.008 in (76.40 mm). The same number in a different style is a different ring, so always quote the style as well as the number.

faqs.q: What are the dimensions of the BX-151 ring joint gasket?
faqs.a: For the BX-151: outside diameter 3.008 in; width 0.379 in; height 0.379 in; width of flat 0.325 in; outside diameter of flat 2.954 in; pressure-passage hole 0.060 in. These are the nominal ring dimensions in inches with millimetres in the size table; confirm the tolerance against your flange groove before ordering.

faqs.q: Can I use an R or RX ring instead of the BX-151 ring joint gasket?
faqs.a: No. The BX-151 fits API 6BX flanges, which have their own groove geometry and make up almost face-to-face, so only the BX ring of the right number seals them. BX rings do not interchange with R or RX rings.

faqs.q: What pressure can the BX-151 ring joint gasket be used at?
faqs.a: API 6BX: 1-13/16″ at 10,000, 15,000 and 20,000 psi. A BX ring is pressure-energised for service up to 20,000 psi on API 6BX flanges. Use the flange rating as the limit for the BX-151.

faqs.q: Which material should I choose for the BX-151 ring joint gasket?
faqs.a: Match the flange and the service: soft iron (D, 90 HB maximum) and low carbon steel (S, 120 HB) suit carbon-steel flanges in general service, while 316 or 304 stainless (S316 or S304, 160 HB) and Alloy 625 (180 HB) suit corrosive and sour service. The BX-151 must always be softer than the flange groove.

faqs.q: Which standards does the BX-151 ring joint gasket meet?

faqs.q: Which other ring numbers sit next to the BX-151 in the same style?

Ring numbers are not interchangeable between sizes, so confirm the flange before ordering. See the [ring joint gasket guide](/blog/ring-joint-gaskets-r-rx-bx) for the full table.

faqs.q: Can a BX-151 ring joint gasket be reused?

faqs.q: How do I choose between R, RX and BX rings when ordering the BX-151?

faqs.q: What does the number in R-38 mean on a ring joint gasket?
faqs.a: R-38 is a Style R ring and the number identifies one ring size and groove. The R-38 has a pitch diameter of 6.188 in (157.18 mm). The same number in a different style is a different ring, so always quote the style as well as the number.

faqs.q: Should I order the R-38 oval or octagonal?
faqs.a: Order the R-38 octagonal for flat-bottom grooves, which are standard on current flanges, and oval only if the groove is round-bottomed, as on some older flanges. An oval ring also seals in a flat-bottom groove.

faqs.q: What pressure can the R-38 ring joint gasket be used at?
faqs.a: ASME B16.5: NPS 4 Class 2500. The ring takes the rating of the flange it seals, so check the flange class and the groove, not the ring alone. Use the flange rating as the limit for the R-38.

faqs.q: Which material should I choose for the R-38 ring joint gasket?
faqs.a: Match the flange and the service: soft iron (D, 90 HB maximum) and low carbon steel (S, 120 HB) suit carbon-steel flanges in general service, while 316 or 304 stainless (S316 or S304, 160 HB) and Alloy 625 (180 HB) suit corrosive and sour service. The R-38 must always be softer than the flange groove.

faqs.q: Which standards does the R-38 ring joint gasket meet?

Ring numbers are not interchangeable between sizes, so confirm the flange before ordering. See the [ring joint gasket guide](/blog/ring-joint-gaskets-r-rx-bx) for the full table.

faqs.q: Can a R-38 ring joint gasket be reused?
faqs.a: No. The R-38 deforms into the groove when the flange is made up, so fit a new ring each time the joint is broken. Clean the groove, check it for damage and do not mix ring styles.
